title: Can any three sticks make a triangle?
hook: Sticks of 2, 3 and 6 cm. Tilt the short ones however you like. Do the ends ever meet?

doesNotKnow: that three lengths make a triangle only if the two shorter add to more than the longest

misconception: Any three sticks can be joined into a triangle if you tilt them the right way.
objective: The learner can say that 2, 3 and 6 cm sticks can never make a triangle, because even lying flat the two short ones reach only 5 cm, and that three lengths close only when the two shorter add to more than the longest.

claims.text: Three lengths a ≤ b ≤ c form a triangle exactly when a + b > c: a straight line is the shortest way between two points, so the two-stick detour must be longer than the base.
claims.source: Triangle inequality (Euclid, Elements I.20); the converse by construction (law of cosines gives a real apex when a + b > c). company/domains/briefs/checks/math-wave-j-check.mjs label G3.
claims.note: Triangle inequality (Euclid I.20: any two sides together exceed the third); the converse is Euclid I.22 / law of cosines: for a+b>c, x=(c²+a²−b²)/2c gives |x|<a, so a real apex exists. Equality gives height 0 (degenerate).

claims.text: For sticks 2, 3 and 6 cm the free ends get no closer than 1 cm, lying flat (2 + 3 = 5 < 6), and raising them only widens the gap; 3, 4, 6 meet above the base (3 + 4 = 7 > 6); 2, 4, 6 meet only lying flat (2 + 4 = 6, height 0). Recall: of 1, 2, 4 / 2, 3, 4 / 2, 2, 4 cm, only 2, 3, 4 makes a triangle.
claims.source: G3 (2,3,6 gap 1; 3,4,6 closes; 2,4,6 flat). Gap with both sticks at angle θ: ends (2cosθ, 2sinθ) and (6 − 3cosθ, 3sinθ); dx = 6 − 5cosθ and dy = sinθ both grow on 0° to 90°, so the gap is least (1 cm) at 0°. 3, 4, 6 apex at x = 29/12 ≈ 2.42 cm, height ≈ 1.78 cm (sticks at 36.3° and 26.4°). Demo.tsx geometry().
claims.note: Re-derived: the free ends lie on circles of radius 2 about (0,0) and 3 about (6,0); the centres are 6 > 5 apart, so the ends are never closer than 1 cm, at any angles (brute-force grid over both angles: min 1.000 at 0°,0°). Equal-angle gap rises monotonically 0°→90° (1.000, 1.743, 2.564, 3.606, 6.083). 3,4,6 apex x=29/12, h=1.778, angles 36.3° and 26.4°; 2,4,6 h=0. Recall: 1+2=3<4, 2+3=5>4, 2+2=4 degenerate; only 2,3,4.

claims.text: For 2, 3 and 6 cm with both short sticks at 45° the gap is 2.6 cm; at 60° it is 3.6 cm.
claims.source: Same gap formula: at 45° √((6 − 5·0.7071)² + 0.7071²) = 2.564; at 60° √(3.5² + 0.866²) = 3.606 (Demo.tsx geometry(), shown to 0.1 cm).
claims.note: Recomputed: 45° → 2.5639 (2.6 cm), 60° → 3.6056 (3.6 cm). Matches the stage readouts in the walkthrough.

recall.question: Which three sticks can be joined end to end into a triangle?
recall.why: The two shorter sticks must add to more than the longest: 2 + 3 = 5 beats 4, but 1 + 2 = 3 falls short and 2 + 2 = 4 only lies flat.
